subject: Literature-in-English
preamble: The Literature-in-English syllabus is designed to evaluate candidates' appreciation of literary works across prose, drama, and poetry. It assesses candidates' understanding of literary techniques, figures of speech, thematic concerns, characterization, stylistic devices, and cultural/historical contexts across African and Non-African prescribed texts, including Shakespearean drama.
aims: Develop candidates' appreciation of literary arts, creative expression, and aesthetic values;
Evaluate competence in analyzing themes, characterization, plot structures, and stylistic devices in prescribed texts;
Enhance critical thinking and literary appreciation through exposure to diverse African and Non-African prose, drama, and poetry;
Examine understanding of Shakespearean drama, universal literary concepts, and unseen literary appreciation.
requirements: Candidates must take all three papers: Paper 1 (Objective & Unseen), Paper 2 (Drama & Poetry), and Paper 3 (Prose).
Candidates are required to study all prescribed texts specified in the official WASSCE 2026–2030 harmonized syllabus.

examination_scheme.summary: The examination consists of three compulsory papers testing literary appreciation, unseen prose and poetry, and set African and Non-African texts across drama, poetry, and prose.

papers.title: Objective and Unseen Test
papers.details: Consists of fifty multiple-choice objective questions covering general principles of literary appreciation, literary terms, unseen prose passages, unseen poems, and general questions on prescribed set texts.

papers.title: Drama and Poetry
papers.details: Consists of essay questions divided into two sections: Section A (African and Non-African Drama) and Section B (African and Non-African Poetry). Candidates answer essay questions based on prescribed texts.

papers.title: Prose and Shakespeare
papers.details: Consists of essay questions divided into two sections: Section A (African and Non-African Prose) and Section B (Shakespearean Text). Candidates answer questions testing thematic, character, and stylistic analysis.

topics.title: 1. Literary Terms and Concepts
topics.notes: Identification and analysis of figures of speech (metaphor, simile, personification, irony, hyperbole, oxymoron, paradox, alliteration, assonance, etc.), drama terms (soliloquy, dramatic irony, catharsis, hubris), poetic forms (sonnet, elegy, ode, ballad, free verse), and narrative techniques (point of view, stream of consciousness, flashback).

topics.title: 2. Unseen Prose and Poetry Analysis
topics.notes: Critical analysis of unseen short prose excerpts and unseen poems, focusing on mood, tone, central theme, imagery, structure, and authorial intention.

topics.title: 1. Shakespearean Drama
topics.notes: Detailed study of 'Antony and Cleopatra' by William Shakespeare, covering historical context, tragic structure, character motivation, political themes, imagery, and dramatic techniques.

topics.title: 2. African Drama
topics.notes: Thematic analysis, dramatic structure, characterization, and cultural background of prescribed African plays: 'Once Upon an Elephant' by Bosede Ademilua-Afolayan and 'The Marriage of Anansewa' by Efua Sutherland.

topics.title: 3. Non-African Drama
topics.notes: Structural, contextual, and thematic study of prescribed Non-African plays: 'An Inspector Calls' by J. D. Priestley and 'A Man for All Seasons' by Robert Bolt.

topics.title: 1. African Prose
topics.notes: In-depth study of plot, narrative perspective, characterization, setting, socio-political themes, and stylistic devices in prescribed African novels: 'So the Path Does Not Die' by Pede Hollist and 'Redemption Road' by Elma Shaw.

topics.title: 2. Non-African Prose
topics.notes: Analytical study of plot, character development, social commentary, thematic depth, and prose techniques in prescribed Non-African novels: 'To Kill a Mockingbird' by Harper Lee and 'Path of Lucas: The Journey He Endured' by Susanne Bellefeuille.

topics.title: 1. African Poetry
topics.notes: Detailed textual, stylistic, and thematic study of prescribed African poems: 'Once Upon a Time' (Gabriel Okara), 'New Tongue' (Elizabeth L. A. Kamara), 'Night' (Wole Soyinka), 'Not My Business' (Niyi Osundare), 'Hearty Garlands' (S.O.H. Afriyie-Vidza), and 'The Breast of the Sea' (Syl Cheney-Coker).

topics.title: 2. Non-African Poetry
topics.notes: Textual and stylistic analysis, tone, rhythm, and themes in prescribed Non-African poems: 'She Walks in Beauty' (Lord Byron), 'The Nun's Priest's Tale' [shortened] (Geoffrey Chaucer), 'Digging' (Seamus Heaney), 'Still I Rise' (Maya Angelou), 'The Telephone Call' (Fleur Adcock), and 'The Stone' (Wilfred Wilson Gibson).
